newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan may relax controls on foreign shippers.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan may relax controls on foreign shippers.

text.p: Taiwan's transport ministry said on Tuesday it was considering allowing more foreign shippers to establish local branch offices.
"The ministry is evaluating whether to allow more foreign shippers to open branches," a Ministry of Transportation and Communications official told Reuters by telephone.

Taiwan has more than 30 local shipping companies and agents, but only two overseas shippers -- American President Lines Ltd and Sea-Land Service Inc, both of the United States -- have legal branch offices.
Other foreign shippers are allowed to operate only through local joint ventures or representative agents.
Some foreign shippers have applied to establish branch offices in Taiwan but all have been rejected for reasons that have not been made public.
Ministry officials declined to comment in detail why Taiwan had only allowed two U.S. shippers, while rejecting others.
Ministry sources said the U.S. branches' approvals, dating to the 1970s, reflected political and diplomatic considerations.
